item.title: Chikubushima: The Sacred Island of Lake Biwa — Guide
item.description: Chikubushima is the sacred island of Lake Biwa, a steep green islet off the lake’s northern shore that has drawn pilgrims for more than a thousand years as one of Japan’s foremost sanctuaries of Benzaiten, goddess of music, water and fortune. Its stone stairways climb from the ferry dock through Hogonji temple — a stop on the Saigoku Kannon pilgrimage — to Tsukubusuma Shrine, whose National Treasure worship hall and the ornate Karamon gate preserve carvings and structures transferred from Toyotomi Hideyoshi’s vanished Fushimi Castle, and visitors cast kawarake clay discs from the cliff-edge toward a torii below, a wish granted if the disc sails through.
